source.title: VIST3A: Text-to-3D by Stitching a Multi-view Reconstruction Network to a Video Generator
source.authors: Hyojun Go; Dominik Narnhofer; Goutam Bhat; Prune Truong; Federico Tombari; Konrad Schindler

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. The text identifies it as published at ICLR 2026.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether representations from independently pretrained models can be connected by a linear stitching map and retain useful downstream performance. This is a different method and setting from the original sources.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the linear stitching and reconstruction evaluations, and the comparison of MSE and CKA as indicators of layer transferability. Text-to-3D benchmark results and cited claims about prior model stitching are not treated as results about representation convergence.
record.test_reason: This is a text-to-3D methods paper, but it reports whether independently pretrained video VAE encoders can be stitched, via a linear layer, to 3D reconstruction networks with little loss. That bears on V4 in a new setting: video VAE latents to MVDUSt3R, VGGT and AnySplat layers. Big caveat: every stitched result is reported after 50 epochs of LoRA finetuning of the stitch and downstream layers, plus register and class tokens for VGGT and AnySplat. No linear-only, pre-finetune performance is reported. The CKA-versus-MSE layer comparison bears weakly on V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that a video VAE's latents can be linearly stitched to an early layer of an independently pretrained 3D model. After lightweight self-supervised finetuning, this preserves 3D reconstruction quality, and combined with reward finetuning it yields text-to-3D models that beat prior methods. They find MSE a more reliable layer-selection criterion than CKA in their setting, and that absolute MSE does not predict performance across VAE architectures. Their framing is methodological; they do not claim representation convergence.
record.recipe_differences: Uses least-squares linear stitching and downstream reconstruction evaluation between video VAE latents and 3D reconstruction networks; it does not reproduce the methods of either original source.
record.method_sensitivity: Transferability assessment varies with the similarity measure: CKA is less precise than MSE for layer selection. Absolute MSE across different VAE architectures does not predict performance; stitching layers must be selected for each VAE–3D-model pair.

fits_no_version.finding: Absolute linear-fit MSE across different VAE architectures does not predict downstream stitched performance, although relative MSE within one VAE does.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear-map residual between two models predicts functional stitchability only within a fixed source model, not across source models.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the relevant table results. Layer-sweep values are primarily shown in figures. The evaluated stitching compatibility is specific to video VAE latents and selected 3D reconstruction models; it does not establish broad interchangeability across model types or tasks.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5 camera-pose metrics are omitted to prioritize pointmap measures of retained reconstruction performance. Text-to-3D generation benchmarks unrelated to the stitching compatibility question are also omitted.

untested.parts: Performance of a pure linear stitch without finetuning; relative representations; unpaired-data mapping; settings outside video-VAE-to-3D-encoder pairs.
No interpretable feature or circuit analysis.
Input variation, out-of-distribution data, neighbourhood-based measures.
No test of how complete alignment is beyond small linear-fit MSE; no analysis of causes such as shared data or objectives.

missing.what: Stitched results for Hunyuan, SVD and CogVid + MVDUSt3R on pointmaps (e.g. 7-Scenes NC mean 0.699 vs 0.730, ETH3D Acc mean 0.405–0.412 vs 0.400)
Minimum linear-fit MSE for MVDUSt3R layers per VAE (0.409, 0.397, 0.461, 0.404), much higher than for AnySplat
The fact that all stitched evaluations follow 50 epochs of LoRA finetuning of S and the downstream layers; no linear-only baseline is reported

record.verdict_notes: The relation is borderline T4, since stitching is a tool for the authors' own method. It is kept as tests (T3) because the paper explicitly reports, as a finding, that independently pretrained models are linearly stitchable with minimal loss. The record's V4 limits_scope label rested on noise-level metric changes and is replaced by layer and finetuning dependence. Several baseline medians in R4–R6 were copied from the wrong rows.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model scale or capability, and no test of alignment across increasingly capable models.
No paired image-caption representation alignment or vision-language model comparison.
No same-architecture, different-seed comparison or shared-feature/subspace analysis.

Tests linear stitching between a video VAE latent representation and layers of 3D reconstruction models, with downstream reconstruction performance. It does not test relative representations, stitching arbitrary network layers, unpaired-data mapping, or interchangeability across a broad range of tasks.
No recurring interpretable feature, neuron, SAE feature, or circuit analysis.
Compares MSE and CKA and reports that absolute MSE does not predict cross-architecture performance. It does not systematically vary inputs, neighbourhood settings, or out-of-distribution data.

The models are described as independently pretrained, including on different data, but the study does not compare shared-data/objective training against alternatives or test what causes the observed compatibility.

rows.subject: Wan+VGGT
rows.operation_detail: Sweep the VGGT stitching layer and relate linear-stitching MSE to pointmap quality.
rows.measure: Linear stitching MSE and pointmap performance
rows.note: The text says lower stitching residuals correlate with better pointmaps.
rows.check: Figure-only. It shows stitchability depends on layer: the best result is at early layer 2, and deeper layers have higher MSE and worse pointmaps. The stitched decoders here are also finetuned. It does not measure convergence-measure dependence, so it does not bear on V6.

rows.subject: Wan+VGGT
rows.operation_detail: Compare CKA across Wan VAE latents and VGGT layer representations as an indicator of transferability.
rows.measure: CKA and relation to stitching performance
rows.note: The authors say CKA captures overall performance degradation but is less precise than MSE and does not identify layer 2 as the best-performing layer.
rows.check: CKA and MSE agree on the overall trend across layers but differ on the best layer (CKA misses layer 2). This is only weak metric dependence. Figure-only. It does not bear on V4.

rows.subject: CogVideoX + AnySplat
rows.operation_detail: Report the minimum linear-transfer MSE for the video VAE and AnySplat layer search.
rows.locator: Figure 10 and accompanying text; Appendix E
rows.note: The paper says this low absolute MSE does not predict cross-architecture performance; Table 3 reports PSNR 21.32.
rows.check: Concerns whether absolute linear-fit MSE predicts finetuned downstream PSNR across VAEs. That is not a convergence measure varying with metric or inputs. The text and the Fig. 10 caption disagree on which pair has the lowest MSE.

relationships.condition: Wan, Hunyuan, SVD and CogVideoX VAE latents stitched linearly to early layers of MVDUSt3R, VGGT and AnySplat, followed by LoRA finetuning
relationships.reason: Stitched models keep pointmap quality nearly unchanged (R1-R12) and match or slightly exceed AnySplat NVS (R13-R24). This holds only after finetuning.
relationships.display_finding: After LoRA finetuning, stitched models kept pointmap quality nearly unchanged and matched or slightly exceeded AnySplat novel-view synthesis.

relationships.condition: Choice of stitching layer, and reliance on finetuning
relationships.reason: Interchange works only at early 3D-encoder layers; deeper layers give higher MSE and worse pointmaps (R25). All performance numbers are post-finetune, so the loss from the linear map alone is not shown (text, Sec. 3.1 and App. C.1).
relationships.display_finding: Early 3D-encoder stitches worked, while deeper stitches increased mean squared error and worsened pointmaps; reported performance followed finetuning and did not isolate the linear map's loss.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Choice of stitching layer, and reliance on finetuning
source_check.reason: Figure 5 supports qualification by stitching layer: lower residuals yield better pointmaps, with best performance at layer 2. Finetuning is part of the evaluated condition; its necessity is untested. The text establishes better early-layer performance, not categorical impossibility at deeper layers.

relationships.condition: CKA vs linear-fit MSE across VGGT layers against Wan VAE latents

relationships.display_finding: Both measures followed the same overall layer trend but identified different layers as best aligned.

relation.reason: Reports linear-transfer residuals, layer sweeps, and reconstruction comparisons with original models, directly bearing on V4 and V6.

tranche.reason: Tests stitching and metric-dependent layer selection in a new video-VAE-to-3D-reconstruction setting.

source_check.notes: Evaluations use adapted decoders, not frozen linear-only stitches; VGGT and AnySplat also receive token adaptation. The supplied text is arXiv v2, dated 5 March 2026, published at ICLR 2026.

statements.correction: Stitched-decoder evaluations follow adaptation of the stitching layer and downstream model using LoRA. Frozen linear-only reconstruction loss is unreported; finetuning necessity is untested. Layer dependence qualifies V4's scope.
statements.problem: The finetuning caveat is accurate, but an untested linear-only stitch does not establish a challenge to V4.
